highlights.title: Ark's Wood Favors Nvidia, AMD in 'Volatile' Chip Cycle
highlights.description: Cathie Wood, founder, CEO and CIO of Ark Investment Management, discusses why she avoids traditional memory-chip players, saying the business cycle is "most volatile." Speaking on Bloomberg Television, Wood adds that we are "just at the beginning" of the artificial intelligence revolution. "In terms of our semiconductor exposure, [we] tend to be at the less-cyclical end of the spectrum," she adds. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: DeepL CEO on Voice AI Growth and Competition
highlights.description: DeepL CEO Jarek Kutylowski discusses surging demand for voice-to-voice translation and how AI is transforming global business. He also addresses competition with OpenAI and Anthropic, DeepL’s AWS strategy, European data sovereignty, recent workforce cuts and why the company is comfortable remaining private. He spoke with Bloomberg’s Tom Mackenzie, at the International AI Summit in Dublin, Ireland. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: MAIA: Interview of Guillaume Princen on Anthropic’s AI Strategy
highlights.description:
In an interview on October 14, 2026, Anthropic’s Head of International Startups & Digital Native, Guillaume Princen, discussed how startups and major firms are adopting Anthropic’s AI, including Claude tools, to boost employee productivity, overhaul processes, and build new products. He highlighted growing demand for frontier models like Opus 5.5, now about 40% cheaper than its predecessor, and a shift toward using different models for specific tasks across the 5.5 family. Princen emphasized Anthropic’s safety-first approach versus open-source and open-weight competitors, underscoring third-party auditing, closer cooperation with governments, and willingness to delay or limit powerful model releases—such as with Methos—if safety concerns arise, even at the expense of near-term revenue.

highlights.title: ASML Raises Full-Year Sales Outlook
highlights.description: ASML upgraded the low end of its 2026 sales forecast as increasing artificial intelligence spending boosts demand for the Dutch company’s chip-making machines. The firm projected annual sales of between €44 billion ($49 billion) and €45 billion this year. ASML's outlook offers an indication of investment plans by chipmakers like TSMC, Samsung Electronics and Intel. Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
